sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Income-Generating Real Estate Property Portfolio Trust (REIT)

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg-United States Income and Capital Tax Treaty (signed 3 April 1996)
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) free movement rights
General Agreement on Trade in Services (GATS) commitments

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 13 January 2019 establishing a Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended; Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (2020, 2021, 2023); Luxembourg Anti-Money Laundering Regulation of 1 February 2024; Commission of the Supervisory Authority of the Financial Sector (CSSF) Regulation No. 23-01 on AML/CFT supervision; supplemented by CSSF Circulars 18/690, 19/716, and 21/744.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized partnership agreement (Convention de Société) or notarial deed of incorporation for asset contributions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary (Notaire) or foreign notary when executing contribution of foreign real estate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (where the deed is executed abroad and subsequently filed in Luxembourg)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Non-Confusion (Certificat de Non-Confusion) issued by the Luxembourg Business Registers
Certificate of Good Standing (Extrait du RCS or foreign equivalent) for each corporate general partner or shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg RCS or competent foreign company registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passports or identity cards for all legal and beneficial owners, managers, and signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority (e.g., Immigration or civil registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if required by Luxembourg notary or financial institution)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for incorporation formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Duly executed by the principals before a notary or sworn translator

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all beneficial owners, directors, managers, and authorized signatories against the CSSF PEP list, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (EU Regulation 269/2014 and 2580/2001), UN Security Council Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List and Denied Persons List, Interpol Red Notices, the Luxembourg RBE registry, and the EU register of beneficial ownership. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP or high-risk third-country validator. Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) structure triggers specific requirements under Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 (Art. 3-2) and CSSF Circular 21/744 regarding beneficial ownership of assets held through trusts or similar legal arrangements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Latin script. The RCS accepts French, German, or Luxembourgish textual elements, but the name must be sufficiently distinguished from existing registrations. Foreign-language names (including English) are permissible if rendered in Latin characters and accompanied by a French or German translation of any descriptive components. The use of 'S.C.Sp.', 'SCSp', or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' as the statutory suffix is mandatory.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected by the LBR, the applicant may request an administrative review by making a written application to the Director of the Luxembourg Business Registers within 15 days of the rejection notice. The application must provide evidence of distinctiveness, alternative search results, and any legal basis for the name. If the internal review fails, the applicant may appeal to the Tribunal d'Arrondissement de Luxembourg (District Court) by filing a substantive motion within 30 days of the final rejection. A name reservation may be extended for one additional period of 60 days prior to expiry by filing an extension request on the LBR portal and paying the applicable fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are not permissible as the sole registered office for an SCSp in Luxembourg. The registered office must be a physical address in Luxembourg, which may be provided by a licensed domiciliation agent (société de domiciliation autorisée) if the company does not have its own premises. The domiciliation agent must comply with the Law of 13 January 2019 and CSSF Circular 19/716. For a real estate investment trust (REIT) SCSp, the Luxembourg place of effective management or a permanent establishment must exist to maintain substance, and the registered office must be capable of receiving official notifications and conducting investor meetings.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate (35%±10%): Luxembourg RCS and the CSSF may conduct unannounced on-site inspections under CSSF Circular 23-01, especially if the SCSp acts as an alternative investment fund manager (AIFM) or holds real estate assets requiring a license. The CSSF has discretion to verify substance, office presence, books and records, and AML/CFT procedures.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name reservation and Certificate of Non-Confusion (LBR fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (LBR fee schedule as amended; approximately EUR 39 for the name reservation)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of partnership agreement (Convention de Société) for the SCSp
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff under Luxembourg Law of 9 December 1976 (honoraria based on notarial complexity and transaction value)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and notarial legalization for corporate documents issued outside the EU
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent competent authority of the country of origin (e.g., Secretary of State, Foreign Ministry)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per jurisdiction (USD 50-150 per document)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the partnership agreement, revised in compliance with Luxembourg law and ISIC 6499 REIT requirements
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Luxembourg attorney (avocat à la Cour)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (hourly rate approx. EUR 300-500 per hour; standard drafting package)
Statutory registration fee (approximately EUR 90 + EUR 10 electronic filing fee)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of incorporation in the Recueil Electronique des Sociétés (RES)
UBO declaration and initial registration in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: RBE filing fee as set under the Law of 13 January 2019 (approximately EUR 40)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed domiciliation services (renewable annually) at Luxembourg registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed domiciliation agency (société de domiciliation autorisée)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for SCSp real estate holding structures (EUR 1,500 - EUR 3,000 per year)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT and PEP/Sanctions screening of UBOs, directors, and managers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External compliance provider or Luxembourg attorney (professional fees)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for individual LexisNexis/Dow Jones screens plus AML risk assessment (hourly or per-screen fee)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Foreign legalization of internal corporate resolutions and appointment of a Luxembourg manager
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary in country of origin and any competent embassy/consulate, if not covered by Apostille
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular fee schedule and notarial tariff of the foreign jurisdiction

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial substance and physical office documentation for CSSF inspection readiness
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Local corporate service provider (e.g., corporate secretarial firm)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for substance preparation, minutes, and records localisation (USD 800-1,500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency reserve for administrative rejections or appeals
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Internal contingency benchmark (5-10% of total pre-incorporation estimated costs)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies as amended (for the Société en Commandite Spéciale, Part IV, Sections 101-110); Law of 23 July 2016 on the SCSp implementing the special limited partnership regime; Law of 19 December 2002 governing the RCS and electronic filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS) acting through the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) e-platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation form in the form of the 'Declaration d'Inscription' filed electronically via the eJustice/e-Procurement portal, accompanied by the limited partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; partners are free to determine the capital contributions in the limited partnership agreement. No statutory escrow account requirement is imposed by the law on commercial companies; however, if the entity is a regulated real estate investment trust or alternative investment fund, separate capital/escrow rules under the relevant CSSF circular may apply.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, (I) the founding partners hereby subscribe to the partnership interests of Société en Commandite Spéciale as set out in the limited partnership agreement, and that each partner's capital contribution shall be paid in kind or in cash as specified therein; (II) the registered office of the partnership is established at [Address], Luxembourg, with immediate effect; (III) [Name] is appointed as Manager (Gérant) with sole authority to represent the partnership in the ordinary course of business; (IV) the Manager is hereby instructed to file the incorporation application with the RCS, publish the statutory notice in the Recueil Électronique, and undertake all actions necessary for legal existence and compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – online name reservation module on lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an electronic name reservation application for the proposed SCSp name by registering on the LBR portal, providing the exact legal form suffix 'SCSp'. The authority checks whether the name is distinguishable from existing company names and permissible under Luxembourg law (not contrary to public order / misleading).
required_dossiers: Proposed name in full with SCSp suffix
Corporate details draft (legal form, address, purpose)
ID or passport copies of the requester / filer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried, file a new request with an alternative name or submit a written explanation demonstrating distinguishability; the response period is normally 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Signing of Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (if notarisation chosen) or private signing by all founding partners; no legal requirement for notarisation of a non-UCITS SCSp unless real property contributions require a notarial deed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the limited partnership agreement (Contrat de Société) defining the legal form 'Société en Commandite Spéciale', registered office, purpose (real estate investment trust), contributions, profit-sharing rules, management powers, assignment restrictions, and dissolution events. Have all partners sign the agreement in accordance with the Law of 1915. Retain a signed counterpart for the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement (draft final)
Identity and address evidence of each partner (passport / resident permit)
Power of attorney if a representative signs
Statement of capital contributions (schedule)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS later queries the substance of the agreement, the partners may pass a rectification resolution and file an amended agreement; no notarisation backstop is required for pure financial holdings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Incorporation Application with RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) via the eJustice/e-Procurement portal (rbds.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the eJustice portal, select 'RCS Insertion Request', attach the signed partnership agreement and the completed 'Declaration for Legal Entities' form, and submit electronically. The RCS reviews the legal conformity of the filing, especially the jurisdiction clause and the identity of the manager. Following approval, the registration is effective on the date of filing; the RCS issues a certificate of registration and a register number (R.C.S. XXXXX).
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement (signed / notarised if applicable)
Declaration of approval of registered office (Bail à usage professionnel / consent of owner)
Identity and proof of address of every partner (and manager if separate individual)
Certificate of no prior bankruptcy or criminal prohibition for manager
Request for RCS registration (Form Bs)
Proof of identity of filing representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for missing documents or legal defects, the RCS issues a query notice ('Notification de carence'). The applicant has one month to cure the deficiencies; if not cured, the request is deemed void and a fresh filing must be made with a new fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in Electronic Compendium (Recueil Electronique des Sociétés et Associations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) – Legal Publication Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after registration, the RCS automatically publishes a notice of the creation of the SCSp in the Recueil Electronique (R.E.S.A.). The notice contains the corporate name, registered office, legal form, registration number, and details of the general partner / managers. Any subsequent amendment to the articles must also be published.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate (automatically generated)
Copy of the deal mandatory in the R.E.S.A. template
No separate fee beyond the filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication contains inaccuracies, file a request for rectification with the RCS within 15 days; the RCS corrects the entry without a new public call.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement et des Domaines (AED); Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD); Registre National des Entreprises (RNE); Taxation via the Luxembourg Direct Tax Authorities (LuxLeaks automated portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the R.C.S. certificate, apply for a Luxembourg tax number (matricule) from the ACD via the portal 'myguichet.lu' if not automatically generated. Determine whether VAT registration is required because the real estate trust engages in taxable leasing activity (rental of real estate is generally exempt under Luxembourg VAT law, but option for taxation is available under Article 44(1)(j) VAT Law). If the SCSp has employees, register with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS).
required_dossiers: RCS certificate / incorporation deed
Partnership agreement in full
Identity of all principals / beneficial owners (LU registry declaration)
Description of the real estate activities for the tax classification
Powers of attorney for tax advisors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ACD does not issue a stable tax number within 14 days, resubmit the request by courier and contact the ACD's 'Guichet Entreprises'; for VAT issues, appeal the decision within three months to the Director of the AED as per Luxembourg tax procedure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Direction Générale de l'Industrie) and the local commune in which the real estate is located
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) activity declaration under the Luxembourg law of 11 May 2007 (if the entity chooses to be taxed as a REIT), plus a local business operating permit ('Autorisation d'établissement') if actual property management or services are performed on the premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Environmental Protection Agency of the Grand-Duchy of Luxembourg)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class II – Registration / Preliminary declaration. Real estate investment holdings are generally outside the mandatory full EIA list (which covers industrial installations). If the portfolio includes facilities listed in Annex I or II of the EU EIA Directive (as transposed by the Luxembourg environmental code), a full environmental impact assessment may be required for such development projects. The mere renting and passive holding of existing property normally triggers only a simple registration/declaration under the water and waste regulations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance thresholds under the Luxembourg water management law (Law of 19 December 2008): any wastewater discharge must meet the limits set by the Ministry of the Environment (e.g., COD below 125 mg/L, BOD5 below 25 mg/L, TSS below 35 mg/L for trade effluents). For volatile organic compounds (VOC) from building services or installations, the VOC Solvent Emissions Regulation (EU) 2018/2026 as incorporated requires a mass flow of less than 10 kg/h and a concentration below 100 mg C/m³. Waste handling must follow the national waste plan and the traceability obligations under the Waste Management Law of 21 March 2012.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification: obtain a 'certificat de sécurité incendie' from the communal fire brigades (Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours) after inspection of any built property, ensuring compliance with the Luxembourg fire safety standards (NFPA/EN norms). Structural load inspection: submit a structural integrity certificate from a licensed engineer if the property is over 50 years old or subject to major renovation; lease agreements must attach the certificate. Workplace clearance: register any occupied office space with the Labour Inspectorate (Inspection du Travail et des Mines, ITM) and obtain an occupational health clearance (annual meeting, safety plan, and, if applicable, a health-risk assessment) covering indoor air quality and emergency evacuation for any employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: The Luxembourg tax authorities are (i) the Administration des Contributions Directes (Direct Tax Administration / Luxembourg Inland Revenue, ACD), responsible for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, net wealth tax, and personal income tax, and (ii) the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Administration, AEDT), responsible for VAT and registration duties. Both report to the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance. Official portals: www.impotsdirects.public.lu (ACD), aedt.public.lu (AEDT), www.guichet.public.lu / MyGuichet.lu (central e-filing gateway), the e-TVA and e-Space electronic VAT channels, and lbr.lu (Luxembourg Business Registers).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing or investing through a Luxembourg SCSp must (1) register the SCSp with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via the Opoce one-stop shop (RCS immatriculation), obtaining the RCS registration number and the national identification number (matricule) which the ACD and AEDT use as the tax file reference. (2) For VAT, the SCSp, or in the case of an SCSp without legal personality the general partner as statutory representative, must file VAT Form 10 (déclaration d'immatriculation à la taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) with the AEDT through the e-TVA/MyGuichet channel to receive the Luxembourg VAT number (format LU+8 digits). A non-EU-established general partner or foreign operator carrying out taxable supplies or letting Luxembourg real estate has no registration threshold and must register from the first euro and appoint a Luxembourg-resident joint VAT representative (représentant responsable solidaire) where it has no Luxembourg or EU establishment. (3) Because the SCSp is fiscally transparent, it does not obtain an autonomous Luxembourg corporate income tax ID; the general partner maintains the ACD file for the partnership, and non-resident partners are registered with the ACD only upon filing a Luxembourg tax return or where Luxembourg-source allocated income is subject to assessment or withholding.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. The Luxembourg SCSp (Société en Commandite Spéciale, special limited partnership) is fiscally transparent under Luxembourg direct tax law: it is not itself liable to corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal), or net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune). Profits, losses, capital gains, credits, and net-wealth items flow through pro rata to partners and are taxed at partner level in their respective states of residence, or in Luxembourg only to the extent attributed to a Luxembourg permanent establishment or Luxembourg-situated real property. Entity_Level_Taxation therefore does not apply, Tax_Exempt_Zone treatment is unavailable, and the ordinary Territorial_Scope of taxation arises solely at partner level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg law provides no general domestic 'check-the-box' election; transparency of the SCSp is statutory (Law of 12 July 2013 and Article 33-2 et seq. of the Law of 10 August 1915, as amended). The partnership deed may elect whether the SCSp has legal personality or not, with identical fiscal transparency in both cases. Qualifying pooled real-estate funds may elect the 2024 Investment Fund Exemption (Law of 10 July 2024, effective for tax years from 1 January 2025), which exempts eligible funds meeting statutory investor-spread, diversification, and professional-management conditions from Luxembourg CIT, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax. For hybrid planning, ATAD 2 (implemented by Luxembourg laws of 21 December 2017 and 19 December 2019) governs hybrid and reverse-hybrid mismatches: where a foreign investor files a US Form 8832 check-the-box election for the SCSp (transparent or opaque), the ACD respects that foreign classification only where substance and contemporaneous documentation support it, and the resulting Luxembourg treatment must be disclosed in the partnership's annual transparency filings. No statutory election converts the SCSp into an entity-level taxed company.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée / TVA), governed by the amended Law of 12 February 1979 and administered by the AEDT; Luxembourg has no separate GST or sales-and-use tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover (VAT-exclusive) small-enterprise exemption (franchise en base, Art. 57 Loi TVA), below which established suppliers may be relieved from VAT charging and registration. Non-established foreign operators, suppliers of services connected with Luxembourg immovable property, and taxable persons making intra-EU acquisitions have no threshold and must register from the first euro. For intra-EU distance sales of goods and B2C digital services by other EU traders, the EU-wide EUR 10,000 OSS aggregation threshold applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not impose real-time fiscal clearance, government-API invoice stamping, or mandated SAF-T digital reporting for B2B transactions. Since 2022, business-to-government (B2G) e-invoicing is mandatory: suppliers invoicing Luxembourg public-sector entities must transmit structured e-invoices (PEPPOL BIS 3.0; UBL 2.1 or UN/CEFACT CII) through certified PEPPOL access points, using the State's free 'e-Space' exchange platform as an available channel. Invoices must be retained for six (6) years. Under the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) reform agreed in June 2025, Luxembourg will phase in mandatory e-invoicing and digital transaction reporting for intra-EU B2B supplies from 1 July 2030, with domestic B2B e-invoicing aligned in the same window; until the mandatory regime enters into force, paper/PDF invoicing remains valid and no cryptographic stamp, QR code, or clearance API is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 152 of the Loi TVA, supplies of goods physically dispatched or transported out of European Union customs territory are zero-rated (0%) if the supplier obtains and retains the customs export declaration (DES/EXS with Movement Reference Number) and transport evidence showing the goods left the EU within 90 days of supply. Intra-EU B2B supplies (Art. 153 Loi TVA) qualify for 0% only where the customer's valid EU VAT ID is held and the EC Sales List is filed on time. For the SCSp real-estate trust: letting and services connected with immovable property are taxable only where the property is situated, so rental flows from non-Luxembourg real estate are outside Luxembourg VAT rather than zero-rated; Luxembourg commercial property rentals are exempt under Art. 44 Loi TVA, subject to the option to tax under Art. 50 Loi TVA for lettings to taxable persons. Management, advisory, holding, and financing services rendered by the Luxembourg SCSp to non-EU taxable investors are outside Luxembourg VAT scope under the B2B place-of-supply rule (customer location). Real property itself cannot be 'exported' for VAT purposes; only movable assets and qualifying cross-border services can benefit from the 0% rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (SAD; DES/EXS electronic filing) with Movement Reference Number (MRN) evidencing exit from EU customs territory
Transport document: Bill of Lading, CMR consignment note, or Air Waybill, dated and consigned to the non-EU destination
Commercial invoice, packing list, and proof of payment (SWIFT MT103/MT210 or Bank Inward Remittance Certificate) demonstrating foreign-currency receipt and export proceeds repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT conducts targeted substance audits of exporters, VAT refund claimants, and SCSp investment vehicles relying on zero-rating or cross-border VAT treatments. Missing, contradictory, or false substantiation triggers retroactive cancellation of the 0% rate, reassessment at the standard 17% VAT rate with arrears interest, clawback of refunds and VAT credit balances, and administrative fines under Arts. 65–67 Loi TVA, which may reach 100% of the evaded tax. Fraudulent export or refund claims additionally expose the general partner, managers, and investors to criminal prosecution before Luxembourg criminal courts (Art. 101 Loi TVA and the tax-fraud provisions of the Criminal Code), including substantial fines and imprisonment for natural persons, disqualification from public procurement, and revocation of fund-management licenses; cross-border cases may be coordinated with OLAF and Eurofisc. The assessment and prescription window is generally three to five years from the filing due date, extended up to ten (10) years for proven fraud or concealment, and the taxable person bears the full burden of proving the physical export or foreign place-of-supply while retaining the complete evidential bundle for six (6) years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a Eurozone member with full, unrestricted current-account convertibility under EU Treaty Article 63 TFEU and the free movement of capital. No exchange controls apply to capital or current transactions. Profit remittance, dividend distributions, and investor redemptions are free of FX quotas or approvals. The only compliance layers are standard tax withholding mechanics, CRS/FATCA reporting, and financial sanctions screening. For a real estate investment trust structured as an SCSp, all income streams (rents, capital gains, interest) are fully convertible into EUR and may be distributed without restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg maintains no statutory export-proceeds surrender regime and no mandatory conversion ratio or repatriation timeline. All export and service proceeds are freely cross-creditable within the EU payment clearing infrastructure. BCL notification applies only for certain balance-of-payments statistics and does not impose any delivery or conversion obligation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderately viable for ancillary payment flows; CSSF-licensed e-money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions may support account servicing, transaction screening, and SEPA/ACH payments for operational treasury. However, offshore non-EU EMIs are legally restricted from providing banking services without a Luxembourg passport or a valid EU cross-border license under PSD2. Given the size, reputational exposure, and regulatory expectations of a real estate investment trust, a traditional tier-1 bank remains the only fully acceptable venue for capital holding, large inbound/outbound transfers, and FX hedging.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandatory for the initial onboarding of an SCSp, especially when non-resident investors hold significant stakes. CSSF AML circulars and bank internal risk policies require at least one in-person interview with the ultimate beneficial owner or the authorised general partner before opening treasury facilities. Remote video KYC may only be accepted within a CSSF-approved digital onboarding framework and typically only for low-risk structures; for real estate investment trusts, face-to-face verification remains the prevailing market standard.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex corporate ownership chain with multiple non-resident SPVs
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transparency declaration attesting the full ownership chain; certified constitutional documents of every SPV; UBO register extract; notarised resolutions; audited financial statements of intermediate entities; and a Luxembourg legal opinion confirming the partnership structure and non-passive investment purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of wealth related to large real estate acquisition funding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Origin-of-assets evidence such as sales deeds, inheritance instruments, prior investment track record; signed source-of-funds (SOF) declaration; bank references from immediately prior financial institutions; tax returns or tax comfort letter; and independent wealth verification report issued by a regulated third-party service provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO involvement of politically exposed persons (PEPs)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP status declaration; enhanced due diligence questionnaire; independent source-of-wealth verification beyond salary or governmental income; sanctions screening clearance; and a written justification from the risk committee approving continued banking relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume dividend/profit distribution to non-EU investors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax residence certificates; CRS self-certification forms (including Form W-8BEN-E or CRS, as appropriate and W-9 when relevant); FATCA classification; underlying business economic proof; distribution compliance policy demonstrating alignment with anti-money-laundering and sanctions rules.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All capital contributions from foreign investors must be routed via SWIFT MT103, entering the Eurozone through Target2 clearing. The wire must reference the SCSp's IBAN and include a commercial purpose code consistent with the CSSF and Luxembourg statistics framework: typically 'FDI – Equity Capital' or 'Shares and Other Equity' under the EU Balance of Payments classification. Intermediary banks must be OFAC-compliant and pre-vetted for sanctions exposure. Inbound USD, GBP, or CHF funds are converted into EUR via the receiving bank's FX desk under a documented standing instruction, with each transaction subject to standard BCL statistical reporting thresholds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For real estate acquisitions, construction proceeds, and investor distributions, clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for all non-SEPA wire payments, including USD via CHIPS/Fedwire using the bank's correspondent network, and EUR via Target2 or SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT). Domestic and EEA distributions are cleared via SEPA and may use Instant SEPA (SCT Inst) where operational. Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600) and standby credits may be issued for construction, procurement, or acquisition milestones. ACH is acceptable only for payroll and small recurring disbursements under EUR 50,000, subject to bank daily limits.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currencies where deliverable forward liquidity is unavailable
FX swaps for short-term liquidity management with authorised counterparties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner confirmation (confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs) to the Luxembourg RBE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after any change in beneficial ownership; annual confirmation within one month after the anniversary of the original RBE registration or the last annual confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 10,000 (generally EUR 250 per violation); criminal liability for knowingly false declarations; persistent failure may lead to a Public Prosecutor's order and enforced compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and, where applicable, consolidated accounts publication (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via the eJustice portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end (e.g., 31 July for 31 December year-ends) and within one month after partner approval, whichever is later; small civil/non-commercial SCSp pools are generally outside the publication obligation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing exposes the general partner to criminal fines and sanctions; RCS records the unresolved default; three consecutive years of non-filing trigger strike-off (radiation) of the entity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regulatory annual report and prudential/statistical returns (where the SCSp is used as a RAIF, SIF, or alternative investment fund under CSSF supervision)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual report within 6 months of financial year-end; AIFMD Annex IV and CSSF statistical returns as specified in applicable CSSF circulars, generally within 15-30 days after each quarter and annual returns within 2 months
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CSSF supervisory fines and enforcement measures, suspension or withdrawal of fund approvals, marketing passport restrictions, and penalties for AIFM reporting breaches

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit if the SCSp is a commercial undertaking that exceeds two of three criteria: balance-sheet total above EUR 4.4 million, net turnover above EUR 8.8 million, or average headcount above 50; regulated REIT fund vehicles are required to be audited regardless of size
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002) as standard; IFRS as adopted in the EU for consolidated accounts, listed vehicles, and regulated investment funds where required

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner must keep the RBE updated within one month of any change in partners or owners controlling more than 25% of interests or rights; an annual confirmation of the stored UBO data must be filed within one month of the registration anniversary; transfer or issue of partnership interests cannot be reported solely through the annual confirmation and requires immediate updating
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General Partner Resolutions and Manager Decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,700 - 5,500 (typical professional domiciliation/PFS service annual fee)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,500 - 27,000 (EUR 5,000 - 25,000) for a typical small/medium real-estate SCSp; larger regulated REIT funds may exceed this range

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined Luxembourg City headline CIT (17% corporate income tax + 1.19% solidarity surcharge on CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax); SCSp is fiscally transparent, so entity-level corporate income tax is €0 and each partner is taxed at their own residency status.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays or preferential REIT deduction apply; the effective zero-rate at SCSp level derives solely from fiscal transparency. Rental income retains full taxable character in the partners' hands. An option to apply VAT on commercial real estate leasing (Art. 45 VAT Law) improves input VAT recovery but does not alter income tax.
